title: Dotenv files
idea: An environment variable is a named setting your program reads from outside its code. dotenv loads them from a `.env` file into `process.env`.
points: `process.env` holds the environment variables of the running process.
Every value is a string, and a variable already set keeps its value.
Import `dotenv/config` first: it loads `.env` before your other files run.

edges.label: text
edges.caption: dotenv reads the file as text, one `KEY=value` pair per line.

edges.label: copies
edges.caption: It copies each pair into `process.env`. Every value becomes a string.

edges.label: set first
edges.caption: A variable the shell or host already set stays as it is. `.env` never overwrites it.

edges.label: reads
edges.caption: Any file can read `process.env.PORT`, but only after dotenv has run.

code.title: .env.example
code.caption: The settings this project uses. Commit this template; copy it to `.env` and put real values only there.

walk.text: `#` starts a comment. This file is committed, so it holds demo values only.
Where the server listens and where MongoDB runs.
Token secrets and lifetimes. Real secrets belong only in your untracked `.env`.

code.title: Loading the file
code.caption: The demo loads the template by `path`; with no options dotenv reads `.env` in the working directory.

walk.text: A host such as a cloud platform may set `PORT` before your app starts.
Load the file. `quiet` hides dotenv's startup message.
The existing `9000` wins over `8000` from the file.
File values arrive as strings. Convert them yourself when you need numbers.

pitfalls: Never commit `.env`. Commit `.env.example` with demo values, so teammates know the keys.
Restart the server after editing `.env`; dotenv reads the file once, at startup.
Never log `process.env`: it prints every secret.

quiz.why: `import` lines run before the code under them. `reader.js` read `process.env.PORT` before `config()` filled it, so `port` is `undefined`.

takeaway: Settings live in `.env`, load first, arrive as strings, and never get committed.

starters: Why use `.env` files instead of hard-coding settings?
